newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT dips 5.7 pct in early trade.
newsitem.headline: PLDT dips 5.7 pct in early trade.

text.p: Heavyweight Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co fell by 85 pesos, or 5.7 percent, to 1,405 pesos in early trade on Monday on the back of its fall in Wall Street, brokers said.

"The drop of PLDT in New York on Friday reflected serious concern of investors that it may be adversely affected by the proposed reduction in accounting rates by the Federal Communications Commission," said Ricardo Puig, analyst at Peregrine Securities (Phils) Inc.

Brokers said the FCC announced last week that for middle income countries such as the Philippines it was planning to cut accounting rates or the cost of international calls to 38 U.S. cents per minute from $1.00 over a two-year period.

PLDT has a 50-50 revenue sharing scheme with US-based carriers. With more than 50 percent of its income sourced from international calls, the carrier's revenues will be sharply affected, analysts said.

PLDT officials were not immediately available for comment but a source at the National Telecommunications Commission said that implementation of metred domestic calls by next year will cushion the effect of the cut in international rates.
The implementation of metering, where subscribers pay charges for domestic calls depending on the duration, will decongest lines and lead to a more efficient PLDT system, the official said.
At present, PLDT subscribers pay a flat monthly fee regardless of the length of domestic calls.
Some 90,170 PLDT shares changed hands by midsession.
